policy:
## Scope

**This program is for security issues in the Ruby programming language.** Please note that the following are **outside the scope** of this program:
* Websites (including *.ruby-lang.org)
* Third-party applications
* Processing untrusted Ruby source code with RDoc (RDoc is designed to document trusted code and is not intended as a security boundary against malicious input)

Reports about websites may be submitted, but they will never be treated as vulnerabilities under this program. Reports about third-party applications, or about processing untrusted Ruby source code with RDoc, are not accepted and will be closed without further review.

### Bundled Gems
The bundled gems are outside the scope of this program, and reports about them are not accepted here. You can see the list of bundled gems in [bundled_gems](https://github.com/ruby/ruby/blob/master/gems/bundled_gems). Please submit vulnerability reports for those gems directly to their respective repositories (e.g., `https://github.com/ruby/[gem name]/security/advisories/new`). Note that bundled gems are distinct from default gems: default gems are shipped as part of the Ruby distribution and remain in scope for this program.

### Experimental Features
Experimental features are also outside the scope of this program. Any feature that emits a warning under the `:experimental` warning category (i.e. `Warning[:experimental]`) is considered experimental. This includes, but is not limited to, `Ractor`, `Ruby::Box`, `IO::Buffer`, and `Fiber#storage=`. These features are still under active development, so their behavior is expected to change and is not yet covered by our security guarantees. Please report any issues with experimental features to the public bug tracker at [https://bugs.ruby-lang.org/](https://bugs.ruby-lang.org/) instead of through this program.

## Submission Guidelines

We appreciate your contributions to making Ruby more secure. Please note that this is a **vulnerability disclosure program without monetary rewards (bounties)**.

To ensure your report is processed effectively, please keep the following guidelines in mind:

* **Technical Accuracy:** You are responsible for the accuracy of your report. Reports containing obvious contradictions or automated spam will be closed.
* **Conciseness:** Please keep your report brief and focused on technical facts. A simple, reproducible Proof of Concept (PoC) is much more helpful than lengthy explanations. Avoid overstating the severity of the issue.
* **Manual Review:** We expect you to personally review and understand every claim in your report. **Do not submit unverified content generated by automated tools or AI.** Submissions that appear to be raw, unverified AI output will be disregarded.

## Vulnerability Handling Process

The Ruby core team and security maintainers have the final decision on which issues constitute security vulnerabilities. We ask that you respect their technical judgment throughout the coordination process.

CVE assignment, if any, is at the sole discretion of the Ruby core team and security maintainers, and is not guaranteed for any report.

**Please note that we do not offer monetary payouts for vulnerability discoveries.** Your contributions are recognized through the improvement of the Ruby ecosystem and, where applicable, public acknowledgment in security advisories.

## Safe Harbor

Any activities conducted in a manner consistent with this policy will be considered authorized conduct and we will not initiate legal action against you. If legal action is initiated by a third party against you in connection with activities conducted under this policy, we will take steps to make it known that your actions were conducted in compliance with this policy.
